column29: Description

Kick-off meeting to go through the NeuonAI project scope, agree on team roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master) and working norms.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Team has read the project scope and agreed on the four focus areas
* Product Owner and Scrum Master confirmed
* Communication channels and meeting cadence agreed

Scaffold the monorepo structure and get it ready for the team to start Sprint 1 workstreams.

* {{apps/mobile}} — Expo blank template, SDK 57, plain JS, Android-only
* {{apps/web}} — React + Vite, plain JS, ESLint with react-hooks rules (no React Compiler)
* {{services/api}} — Express scaffold
* Placeholder folders for {{apps/firmware}}, {{services/anomaly-detection}}, {{packages/api-contract}}, {{infra/mosquitto}}, {{infra/supabase}}, {{docs/*}}
* Root {{.gitignore}} covering {{.env}}, certs/keys, {{node_modules}}, build output, {{.expo/}}, {{.pio/}}, Python venvs
* {{.gitattributes}} for consistent line endings
* {{.github/workflows/ci.yml}} — lint + build check for {{apps/web}}
* {{.github/CODEOWNERS}} — placeholder, needs real GitHub handles before the 2-approval rule on {{packages/api-contract}} can be enforced
* {{CLAUDE.md}} and {{README.md}} with project context, stack, conventions

Remaining before this can close: first commit + PR (branch-per-task, PR review required, never push to {{main}}).

column1: Set up live document for System Design Proposal (Google Docs)
column29:
Create the shared Google Doc for the System Design Proposal with the agreed section headings so everyone can write in parallel.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Doc created with all proposal section headings
* All 7 members have edit access
* Link shared with the team

Split the System Design Proposal sections across the 7 team members and record who owns what.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Every proposal section has one owner
* Workload is roughly balanced across members
* Each section has a matching Jira task assigned to its owner

Write the Background section of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* Current manual plant documentation practice at Niah National Park (handwritten records, physical tags, later data entry)
* The two problem statements: manual/inefficient documentation, and limited digital access to biodiversity knowledge
* Industry partner context: NeuonAI as SFC's commercialisation partner

*Acceptance criteria*

* Section drafted in the proposal doc
* Problem statements match the project scope
* Sources cited

Write the Scope and Stakeholder sections of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* In-scope: the four required focus areas (mobile ground-truthing, web knowledge system, cybersecurity/SSDLC, IoT plant protection) and whether the optional innovation objective is included
* Out-of-scope items (e.g. production IoT hardware)
* Stakeholders: NeuonAI, SFC, botanists, conservation officers, system admins, park visitors, tutor

*Acceptance criteria*

* Scope boundaries clearly stated
* Each stakeholder listed with their interest/role in the system

Write the Deliverables section of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* Software deliverables: mobile app, web knowledge system, API/database, IoT prototype + dashboard
* Security deliverables: SSDLC plan, vulnerability assessment test plan, results, remediation and reassessment evidence
* Documentation deliverables: proposal, final report, presentation/demo

*Acceptance criteria*

* Every deliverable maps back to an objective in the project scope
* Rough timing (which sprint) noted for each

Produce the system design diagrams for the System Design Proposal.

*Suggested set*

* System architecture (mobile, web, API, Supabase, MQTT broker, ESP32 nodes)
* Use case diagram for the four roles (Botanist, Conservation Officer, System Admin, Visitor)
* Data flow / offline sync flow (capture, local SQLite, sync, review/approve)
* ERD for the core entities (specimens, observations, users/roles, sensor nodes, telemetry, alerts)

*Acceptance criteria*

* Diagrams inserted into the proposal doc with captions
* Consistent with the tech stack in README.md
* Editable source files saved in docs/

Write the Alternative Solutions section of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* Alternatives considered for key decisions (e.g. native vs cross-platform mobile, Supabase vs other backends, MQTT vs HTTP for telemetry, pre-printed QR tags vs on-demand generation)
* Pros/cons of each and why the chosen option was selected

*Acceptance criteria*

* At least two alternatives compared per major decision
* Justification links back to project constraints (offline-first, cost, team skills)

Write the Quality Management section of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* Quality standards and how they are checked (PR review required, branch-per-task, CI lint/build, two approvals for api-contract changes)
* Testing approach (unit, integration, field/offline testing, security testing)
* Definition of Done for stories

*Acceptance criteria*

* Section drafted in the proposal doc
* Matches the conventions actually set up in the repo

Write the Resources section of the System Design Proposal.

*Should cover*

* People: the 7 team members and their roles
* Hardware: ESP32-CAM nodes, sensors, Android test devices, printed QR tags
* Software/services: Supabase, Mosquitto, GitHub, Jira, Expo, hosting, and any costs

*Acceptance criteria*

* All required resources listed with estimated cost where relevant
* Any items needing purchase or sponsor approval flagged

Supabase Auth (JWT) verification and role-based access control in the Express API for the four roles: Botanist, Officer, System Administrator and unauthenticated Visitor.

All authorisation is enforced *at the API layer, never in the client*. Stateless JWTs, not session cookies.

*Subtasks*

* CTIP-40: Backend Authentication (Supabase Auth, JWT)
* CTIP-41: Backend RBAC & Testing

The mobile and web login screens were split out on 13 Oct 2026 into their own stories: CTIP-42 (mobile) and CTIP-43 (web). Client sign-in, session caching and token refresh are tracked there.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [x] API accepts Supabase Auth access tokens (JWT)
* [x] Middleware verifies the JWT signature and expiry on every protected route
* [x] Role is read from a trusted claim ({{user_role}}, added by the access token hook), not from the request body
* [x] Each route declares which roles may access it; unauthorised requests get 401/403
* [x] Visitor-only public endpoints work without a token
* [x] Tests cover each role hitting allowed and forbidden routes
* [x] Expired tokens get {{401 TOKEN_EXPIRED}}, so clients know to refresh

Delivered in PR #12 (merged 12 Oct 2026).

*Before deploying:* turn on the custom access token hook in the hosted Supabase project (Authentication > Hooks).

column1: Mobile: Sync Queue Upload with Idempotency Keys
column29:
Upload the local record queue ({{apps/mobile/src/db/}}) to the API once connectivity returns, without ever losing or duplicating a field record.

Silent loss or duplication of field records is the single worst failure mode in this system: those observations are irreplaceable. Server-assigned IDs with client-side idempotency keys. Scheduled last in Sprint 2 (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026).

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* The rest is now separate stories: CTIP-66 resumable photo upload, CTIP-67 conflict handling, CTIP-68 sync status and triggers.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Every queued record carries an idempotency key; retrying never creates duplicates
* The server-assigned ID is written back to the local record after upload
* Records are only removed from the queue after the server confirms
* Tested with the network dropped mid-sync

column1: Mobile: QR Code Generation for Plant Records
column29:
As a botanist, I want to generate a QR code for a plant record when no pre-printed tag is available, so every documented plant can still be tagged and viewed later.

Pre-printed tags (CTIP-15) are the main path; this is the fallback required by the scope ("Generate a QR code for each plant record").

*Acceptance criteria*

* Botanist can generate a QR code for any record, including offline
* QR encodes a stable tag ID / URL, not the plant data itself
* QR can be shared or saved as an image for printing
* Scanning the generated QR opens the record in the app, and the public plant page (CTIP web story) for visitors
* Tag IDs are unique and cannot clash with pre-printed tags

Turn the crash-safety draft cache (CTIP-57) into a proper local record store in {{apps/mobile/src/db/}} ({{expo-sqlite}}), so records are kept on the device before any network call.

*Schedule last in Sprint 2* (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026). Pairs with CTIP-16, which syncs this store.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* Airplane-mode capture is now CTIP-83; offline species search is CTIP-84.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Every submitted record is saved locally first, with a client-generated ID, before any network call
* The local schema is versioned with migrations, so app updates don't wipe unsynced records

column1: Web: Change Roles & Approve New Accounts
column29:

As a system administrator, I want to switch off an account, so someone who leaves cannot keep using the system.

*Note:* the role sits inside the login token, so a deactivated user keeps access until their current token expires (up to about an hour by default). Either document that delay or also check {{is_active}} on sensitive routes.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Admin can deactivate a user
* A deactivated user gets no role in new tokens, so their access stops
* The delay before an existing token stops working is documented or removed
* Deactivation is logged with who did it and when

Write the vulnerability assessment test plan required by the scope's Application Security Aspect.

* Tester(s) are not the people who implemented the code under test

column1: Security: Data Encryption at Rest and in Transit
column29:
Encrypt sensitive data across all platforms, as required by the scope (Objective 3).

*Acceptance criteria*

* All client-to-API traffic uses HTTPS; HTTP is rejected or redirected
* MQTT uses TLS (see CTIP-17)
* Personal data (names, emails, contact details) encrypted at rest in the database
* Local SQLite database on the mobile device is encrypted
* Secrets and keys are kept in environment variables / secret storage, never in the repo
* Approach documented in docs/security/

* Each fix implemented following the written recommendation
* Each Bug links the PR that fixes it
* All High and Critical findings fixed before the reassessment

column1: API: Shared API Client for Web & Mobile
column29:
One small, shared way for the web and mobile apps to call the Express API, so each feature story does not rebuild token handling and error handling on its own.

Rewritten on 13 Oct 2026. Signing in is CTIP-42 (mobile) and CTIP-43 (web); each feature's own API calls stay in its own story (for example CTIP-28, CTIP-26, CTIP-58). They all use this client.

*Tasks*

* An API client module in {{apps/web/src/}} and one in {{apps/mobile/}} (or one in {{apps/shared/}} if it works for both)
* Read the API base URL from the app's {{.env}} (never hard-coded)
* Attach the signed-in user's Supabase access token to every request
* On {{401 TOKEN_EXPIRED}}, refresh the Supabase session once and retry the request
* Turn the API's {{{ code, message }}} errors into one consistent message for the user, including {{403 ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE}}
* Set the API's {{CORS_ORIGINS}} for the web app's address

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Web and mobile both call the API through the shared client, with the base URL taken from {{.env}}
* [ ] Every request carries the current user's access token; public routes work without one
* [ ] An expired token is refreshed and the request retried once, without the user noticing
* [ ] API errors are shown consistently from {{{ code, message }}}
* [ ] The web app can call the API from its local dev address without CORS errors
* [ ] A short usage note in the client file shows how a feature story calls it

As the IoT and web teams, we need realistic sensor data without depending on the physical ESP32 node, so ingestion, anomaly detection (CTIP-38) and the dashboard (CTIP-39) can be built and tested before the hardware is ready.

Python simulator in {{services/anomaly-detection/}}. It mimics the real node: an ESP32 with a DHT11 (temperature, humidity), a YL-69 (soil moisture) and an HC-SR04 (distance, also used for motion detection). Images come from the laptop webcam script (CTIP-17), so the simulator does not need to produce them.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Simulator publishes temperature, humidity, soil moisture, {{distance_cm}} and {{motion_detected}} readings over MQTT/TLS in the same format as the firmware (CTIP-17), or calls {{POST /telemetry}} directly; {{lat}}/{{lng}} optional, to test GPS-equipped nodes
* [ ] Can run several virtual nodes at a configurable interval
* [ ] Can inject disturbance events on demand (motion burst from a sudden distance change, sudden temperature change, soil drying out, node silent)
* [ ] Telemetry is stored in the database and linked to the node and nearby specimen
* [ ] Run instructions in the folder README (PowerShell, {{python}}, {{.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1}})

column1: IoT: ESP32 Sensor Readings & Safe Wiring
column29:
Arduino IDE firmware for the ESP32 sensor node: read the environment around a protected plant.

*Hardware:* ESP32 with a DHT11 (temperature and humidity), a YL-69 (soil moisture) and an HC-SR04 (ultrasonic distance). No camera and no GPS module; the node's location is recorded once, at registration.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* The rest is now separate stories: CTIP-59 motion detection, CTIP-60 MQTT/TLS publishing, CTIP-61 MQTT bridge, CTIP-62 laptop webcam images.

*Progress:* the database side (sensor fields, telemetry matching, image table) was merged on 8 Oct (PRs #4, #5). The firmware itself has not been committed yet.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Firmware committed as {{apps/firmware/sensor_node/sensor_node.ino}}
* [ ] Node reads temperature and humidity (DHT11, at most about once a second), soil moisture (YL-69, converted to percent) and distance (HC-SR04) at a configurable interval
* [ ] YL-69 on an ADC1 pin (GPIO 32 to 39) and powered from a GPIO only while reading
* [ ] HC-SR04 echo through a voltage divider, or the 3.3 V HC-SR04P
* [ ] Board package and libraries listed with versions in {{apps/firmware/README.md}}
* [ ] Wi-Fi and MQTT credentials in a gitignored {{secrets.h}}; nothing secret committed

column1: IoT: Threshold Alert Rules per Node
column29:
As a conservation officer, I want an alert raised automatically when a sensor reading breaks a rule, so the team can respond quickly to possible poaching or habitat disturbance.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* The rest is now separate stories: CTIP-75 statistical model, CTIP-76 node-silent alert, CTIP-77 notifications, CTIP-78 acknowledge and resolve.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Threshold rules configurable per node: motion, distance change ({{thresholds.distance_change_cm}}), sudden temperature or humidity change, soil drying out
* [ ] A rule breach creates an alert with node, specimen, reading, severity and the captured image if available
* [ ] Rules run in the API when telemetry arrives

column1: IoT: Sensor Node Registration & Alert Routing
column29:
As a system administrator, I want to register sensor nodes and decide who receives their alerts, so each node is tied to the specimen it protects and the right officers are notified.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Admin can register, edit and deactivate a sensor node (ID, location, linked specimen)
* Registering a node issues its own MQTT credentials; deactivating revokes them
* Node GPS position is tracked, and a node moving outside its expected area is flagged
* Admin can set which officers receive alerts per node or per severity
* Only the System Administrator role can access these screens and endpoints

Detect physical disturbance near a protected plant with the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor.

Split from CTIP-17 on 13 Oct 2026.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Between published readings, the node samples distance every few hundred milliseconds
* [ ] {{motion_detected}} is set when the distance changes by more than a configurable threshold
* [ ] Single out-of-range or timed-out pings are ignored
* [ ] The latest {{distance_cm}} is sent with each reading so the server can check it

Location: {{apps/firmware/sensor_node/}}

Send each sensor reading securely from the ESP32 to the Mosquitto broker.

Split from CTIP-17 on 13 Oct 2026.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Each reading is published as one JSON message to {{nodes/{node_id}/telemetry}}, matching {{TelemetryReadingInput}} in the API contract
* [ ] Telemetry goes over MQTT with TLS to Mosquitto ({{infra/mosquitto/}}); plain-text connections are rejected
* [ ] Each node authenticates with its own credentials
* [ ] The node reconnects automatically after Wi-Fi or broker loss
* [ ] No certs, keys or Wi-Fi passwords are committed ({{secrets.h}} is gitignored)

A backend subscriber that takes readings from the broker and forwards them to the API, so validation, storage and alert rules live in the API only.

Split from CTIP-17 on 13 Oct 2026. The database side is ready (PRs #4 and #5). {{POST /telemetry}} currently returns 501 in the API.

*Open decision:* where the bridge lives ({{services/api}} or {{services/anomaly-detection}}) has not been decided yet. Agree it with the team before starting.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] The bridge subscribes to {{nodes/{node_id}/telemetry}} (TLS, QoS 1) and forwards each reading to {{POST /telemetry}}
* [ ] {{POST /telemetry}} checks the {{X-Sensor-Key}} header (one shared key from the API's {{.env}} for now; per-device keys come with CTIP-48)
* [ ] Readings are validated against the contract and stored, linked to the node and the specimen it protects
* [ ] Invalid readings are rejected and logged

column1: IoT: Laptop Webcam Capture & Image Upload
column29:
Use a laptop webcam as the sensor node's camera, since the ESP32 has none.

Split from CTIP-17 on 13 Oct 2026. The image table and private bucket are ready (PR #5).

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] A capture script on the laptop takes a photo when the node reports motion
* [ ] The raw JPEG (2 MB maximum) is uploaded to {{POST /sensor-nodes/{id}/images}} over HTTP
* [ ] Images are stored in the private {{sensor-images}} bucket, linked to the node

Flag unusual readings that simple thresholds miss.

Split from CTIP-38 on 13 Oct 2026. Python with scikit-learn in {{services/anomaly-detection/}}. No deep learning: there is no labelled dataset of real disturbance events.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] A lightweight statistical model flags readings outside a node's normal range
* [ ] A flagged reading creates an alert in the same way as the threshold rules
* [ ] Tested with disturbance events from the sensor simulator (CTIP-47)
* [ ] Run instructions in the folder README (PowerShell, {{python}}, {{.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1}})

Treat a node that stops reporting as a possible disturbance.

Split from CTIP-38 on 13 Oct 2026.

*Acceptance criteria*

* A node silent for longer than a configurable time raises an alert
* The node is shown as online again when readings resume

Tell the right people quickly when an alert is raised.

Split from CTIP-38 on 13 Oct 2026. Recipients follow the alert routing from CTIP-48.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Officers are notified (in-app, email or push) within a short delay of an alert
* Recipients follow the routing set up in CTIP-48
* Notifications never include exact plant coordinates (threat model: no plant data or coordinates are emailed)

Let officers work an alert through to the end.

Split from CTIP-38 on 13 Oct 2026. The endpoints are already in the contract and the route permissions ({{/alerts/{id}/assign}}, {{/acknowledge}}, {{/resolve}}, {{/notes}}), but they return 501.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Alerts can be assigned, acknowledged and resolved through the API
* Notes can be added, and the full history is kept
* Only Officer and Admin can do this (already enforced by the route permissions)

Mobile app shell and the botanist's login screen, signing in through Supabase Auth.

Split out of CTIP-14 on 13 Oct 2026 so the backend auth work could close on its own. Builds on the API auth layer from CTIP-14 (Done). API calls, token refresh and error messages come from the shared API client (CTIP-54).

*Scope note:* online-first (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026). "Reconnecting" means a device coming back after being idle, not full offline operation.

*Tasks*

* App navigation and screen structure (done in PR #11)
* Login screen that signs in with Supabase Auth ({{signInWithPassword}}) instead of sample data
* Cache the session on the device and revalidate it when the app reconnects
* Show a clear message for {{403 ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE}} (through CTIP-54)

*Acceptance criteria*

* -App navigation and screen structure in place-
* Botanist can log in on the mobile app through Supabase Auth and receives a JWT
* Session is cached and revalidated when the app reconnects (not full offline auth)
* Logging out clears the session on the device

column1: Mobile: Capture Photos from Camera or Gallery
column29:
As a botanist, I want to take or pick photos for a plant record, so each plant is documented visually.

Split from CTIP-15 on 13 Oct 2026. The Add Plant screen in the mobile prototype (PR #11) already has a photo list, but it uses sample photos.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Photos can be taken with the camera or picked from the gallery
* Several photos can be added to a record and removed before submitting
* Photos stay on the device until the record is submitted
* Location data (EXIF) is stripped from photos before upload (threat model T6)

Location: {{apps/mobile/}}

column1: Mobile: QR Scan to Start or Open a Record
column29:
As a botanist, I want to scan a plant's QR tag to start a new record or open its existing one, so every record is tied to a physical tag.

QR tags are pre-printed and unassigned, and bound to a specimen at scan time. On-demand generation is the fallback (CTIP-27).

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* The rest of the capture flow is now separate stories: CTIP-55 photos, CTIP-56 GPS, CTIP-57 crash-safe draft, CTIP-58 submit to the API.

*Progress:* live camera QR scanning (expo-camera) and scanning from a gallery image are in the mobile prototype (PR #11), but tag lookup uses sample data.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Scanning an unassigned QR tag starts a new record bound to that tag
* Scanning an already-bound tag opens the existing record
* Unknown tags show a clear message
* Tag lookup and binding go through the API, not sample data

Location: {{apps/mobile/}}
column55:
13/Oct/26 10:52 PM;712020:d2164194-82be-4e8b-8a20-373a4106818a;Moved to In Progress. The mobile prototype from [PR #11|https://github.com/Kampung-Semua-Cina/CTIP-biodiversitysystem/pull/11] has:

column1: Mobile: Submission Status & Rejected Record Edits
column29:
As a botanist, I want to see whether my submitted records were approved or rejected by a conservation officer, so I can fix rejected records instead of re-surveying the plant.

Mobile side of the review workflow; the officer's review queue is CTIP-29.

*Acceptance criteria*

* "My submissions" list shows each record's status: submitted / approved / rejected
* Rejected records show the officer's reason
* Botanist can edit a rejected record and resubmit it
* Approved records become read-only for the botanist
* Status refreshes on app open and pull-to-refresh

*Optional / stretch* — scope Objective 5. Only start once the stream's committed Sprint 2 work is done.

Design and build an improvement to the field ground-truthing workflow that makes plant identification, location, recording or management faster, more accurate or more scalable in remote forest conditions. Automated species identification from photos is out of scope (NeuonAI's product).

*Acceptance criteria*

* Limitations of the current ground-truthing workflow identified and written up
* Improved workflow or design proposed and agreed with the team
* Improvement implemented in the app
* Effectiveness evaluated with a suitable test (for example, time per record before vs after)

As a botanist, I want the phone's location saved with each record, so the plant can be found again.

Split from CTIP-15 on 13 Oct 2026. The mobile prototype currently uses a simulated position.

*Acceptance criteria*

* The device's GPS position is captured with each record
* Accuracy in metres is stored and shown to the botanist
* A clear message is shown if location permission is denied

Location: {{apps/mobile/}}

As a botanist, I don't want to lose a half-filled record if the app closes or crashes.

Split from CTIP-15 on 13 Oct 2026. This is a local draft cache only, not a sync queue. Full offline storage is CTIP-44.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] A local SQLite draft ({{expo-sqlite}}) holds taxonomy, morphology, height, notes, photos, GPS and QR tag ID
* [ ] An in-progress draft survives an accidental app close or crash
* [ ] The draft is cleared after a successful submit

Location: {{apps/mobile/src/db/}}

column1: Mobile: Submit Record to API with Retry
column29:
As a botanist, I want my finished record sent to the server, so it reaches the knowledge system.

Split from CTIP-15 on 13 Oct 2026. Online-first: Sprint 1 assumes internet connectivity (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026), so this is a direct submit, not a sync queue.

*Acceptance criteria*

* On submit, the record is sent to the API endpoint defined in the contract
* Each submit carries a client-generated ID / idempotency key, so a retry never creates a duplicate record
* The server-assigned ID is kept with the record after a successful submit
* A failed submit shows an error and lets the botanist retry
* A successful submit is confirmed to the botanist

Location: {{apps/mobile/}}

As a conservation officer, I want to see where each species has been recorded on a map of Niah National Park, so I can understand its distribution.

Leaflet + OpenStreetMap.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* Clustering and filters are now CTIP-70; hiding exact coordinates of endangered species is CTIP-71.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Map shows approved observations for a selected species, or all species, from the distribution endpoint (CTIP-88)
* Clicking a marker shows the record summary and photo

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

column1: Web: Map Marker Clustering & Search Filters
column29:
Keep the distribution map readable and in step with search.

Split from CTIP-31 on 13 Oct 2026. Maps use Leaflet + OpenStreetMap.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Markers cluster when zoomed out
* The map follows the search and filter criteria (CTIP-30)

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

column1: Web: Hide Exact Coordinates of Endangered Species on the Map
column29:
Stop the map from revealing where endangered plants grow to anyone who should not see it.

Split from CTIP-31 on 13 Oct 2026. Threat model T13 and T19. This is a test case in the security assessment.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Exact coordinates of endangered species are shown only to authorised roles
* Other viewers see reduced-precision positions supplied by the API (CTIP-46 distribution endpoint), never trimmed only in the browser

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

column1: Web: Species Soft Delete with Confirmation
column29:
As a conservation officer, I want to remove a species record safely, so mistakes can be undone and history is kept.

Split from CTIP-28 on 13 Oct 2026. The web prototype already soft-deletes on sample data and writes an audit row.

*Acceptance criteria*

* [ ] Delete asks for confirmation
* [ ] Delete is a soft delete ({{is_deleted}}), done through the API
* [ ] Deleted species are hidden from lists and the public page
* [ ] Only Officer and Admin can delete, enforced by the API

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

column1: Web: Species Photo Upload with Captions
column29:
As a conservation officer, I want to upload several captioned photos for a species, so the knowledge base shows what the plant looks like.

Split from CTIP-28 on 13 Oct 2026. The web prototype already has a photo editor and gallery (PR #7), but it uses sample data.

*Acceptance criteria*

* -Multiple photos can be uploaded per species, each with a caption-
* -File type and size are validated-
* Photos are stored in Supabase Storage through the API (CTIP-46 photo endpoint)

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

Web login page for Officers and Admins, signing in through Supabase Auth, plus a layout for each role.

Split out of CTIP-14 on 13 Oct 2026 so the backend auth work could close on its own. Builds on the API auth layer from CTIP-14 (Done). API calls, token refresh and error messages come from the shared API client (CTIP-54).

* Each role lands on its own layout after login

column1: Web: Species Create, View & Edit via API
column29:
As a conservation officer, I want to add, view and edit plant species records, so the knowledge base stays accurate.

*Record fields:* scientific name, common/local names, full taxonomy, description, ecological characteristics, conservation status, cultural significance.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* Photos are now CTIP-64 and soft delete is CTIP-65.

*Progress:* species catalogue, species and specimen pages are on main (PRs #7, #10), on sample data.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Create, view and edit species records from the web app through the API
* Conservation status selected from a fixed list (IUCN categories)
* Only Officer and Admin can edit, enforced by the API
* Changes record who edited and when

column29:
As a conservation officer, I want a queue of field observations waiting for review, so nothing submitted by a botanist is missed.

*Split on 13 Oct 2026.* Approve, reject and request changes is now CTIP-69. The botanist-facing outcome is CTIP-45.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Queue lists newly submitted observations with photos, GPS on a map and the submitted details
* Data comes from the review endpoints (CTIP-86)
* Only Officer and Admin can open it, enforced by the API

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

As a conservation officer or researcher, I want to search and filter plant records, so I can quickly find the species and observations I need.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Search by scientific or common name, with partial matching
* Filter by family/genus, conservation status, location/zone, date range and approval status
* Results are paginated and sortable
* Filters are reflected in the URL so a search can be shared or bookmarked
* Search is fast enough on the full seed dataset (under ~1 second)

column1: Web: Public Visitor Plant Page (QR Landing)
column29:
As a park visitor, I want to scan a plant's QR tag and see information about it without logging in, so I can learn about the plants I see on the trail.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Scanning a QR tag opens a mobile-friendly public page for that plant
* Shows common and scientific name, photo, description, conservation status and cultural significance
* No login required; only public fields are returned by the API
* Coordinate precision reduced server-side for endangered specimens (never exact location)
* Unknown or unassigned tags show a friendly "not found" page
* Endpoint is rate-limited to prevent scraping

column1: Web: Approve, Reject or Request Changes on Observations
column29:
As a conservation officer, I want to approve or reject field observations, so only verified data enters the official records.

Split from CTIP-29 on 13 Oct 2026. The botanist-facing outcome is covered by CTIP-45. Uses the review endpoints from CTIP-46.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Officer can approve, reject (with a reason) or request changes
* Approved observations are linked to the correct species and appear in search and maps
* Every decision is logged with the reviewer and a timestamp
* Only Officer and Admin can decide, enforced by the API

Location: {{apps/web/src/}}

Kick off the SSDLC "assess" step: threat model the system ahead of the Sprint 2 vulnerability assessment (which needs to show a real assess, remediate, reassess cycle).

Cover: the four roles and their trust boundaries, offline-first sync (server-assigned IDs + idempotency), IoT telemetry ingestion over MQTT, image upload over HTTP, and the public unauthenticated Visitor QR flow (including that coordinate precision must be reduced server-side for endangered specimens before reaching a public view).

Security implementation and security testing must go to *different people*, so whoever threat-models/tests should not be the one implementing the auth/RBAC or IoT ingestion code.

*Acceptance criteria*

* Data flow diagram with trust boundaries marked
* Threats identified per component using STRIDE (or similar)
* Each threat rated for likelihood/impact and given a mitigation
* Mitigations that need code turned into Jira tickets
* Document saved in docs/security/

*Scope Focus Area 1 — Smart Digital Ground-Truthing Platform* (Objective 1)

Android mobile app ({{apps/mobile}}, Expo) that lets botanists document plant specimens in the field at Niah National Park.

*Connectivity (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026):* built online-first, assuming internet is available in the field, so the whole system works end to end first. Full offline data collection and sync are added at the end of Sprint 2 (CTIP-44, CTIP-16). This differs from the submitted proposal, which stated offline-first as a hard requirement.

*Botanist role must be able to:*

* Register new plant records on site
* Record detailed plant information (taxonomy, morphological characteristics, height, related attributes)
* Capture and attach photographs
* Record GPS location
* Synchronise field data with the central database
* Generate / bind a QR code for each plant record so users can view its details

*Also in scope:* QR scanning of tagged plants, searchable plant species reference, offline data collection (Sprint 2, last).

*Stories:* CTIP-15, CTIP-42 (stream A, Sprint 1); CTIP-26, CTIP-27 (stream B, Sprint 1); CTIP-45, CTIP-51 (stream A, Sprint 2); CTIP-44, CTIP-16 (stream B, Sprint 2).

*Outcome:* botanists and conservation officers identify, document and manage plant records during field surveys with less manual effort and better data quality.

*Scope Focus Area 2 — Digital Plant Knowledge System* (Objective 2)

Web-based biodiversity knowledge system ({{apps/web}}, React + Vite) for managing and accessing plant species information.

*Features:* plant taxonomy and scientific names, species descriptions, botanical photographs, conservation status, species distribution maps, search and filtering by scientific or common name.

*Conservation Officer role must be able to:*

* Add, edit and delete plant species records
* Upload plant photographs and supporting information
* Review and approve submitted observations (from the mobile app)
* Search and filter biodiversity records
* Generate and export biodiversity reports

*Outcome:* conservation officers can manage, retrieve and update accurate biodiversity information to support conservation, research and public education.

*Scope Focus Area 3 — Cybersecurity and Data Protection* (Objective 3)

*Implementation (all platforms):*

* Secure login for all users with simple authentication methods
* Encryption of sensitive/personal data
* Role-based access control (Botanist, Conservation Officer, System Administrator, unauthenticated Visitor)

*Application Security Aspect (assessed deliverables):*

* Project planning and execution based on the Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
* Vulnerability assessment test plan — tools and scope of testing defined
* Vulnerability assessment results with verification of each vulnerability
* Recommendations and their implementation
* Evidence of reassessment showing the vulnerabilities were fixed

*Team rule:* security implementation and security testing must be done by different people.

*Scope Focus Area 4 — IoT-Enabled Plant Protection* (Objective 4)

GPS and environmental sensor nodes (ESP32-CAM, {{apps/firmware}}) deployed near rare or endangered plant species.

*Basic functionalities:*

* Real-time environmental sensing (temperature, humidity, movement)
* GPS-based plant and sensor tracking
* Threat detection and automated alerts for unusual activity (e.g. potential poaching, habitat disturbance)
* Centralised monitoring dashboard for administrators
* Ecological data storage and analysis

*Out of scope:* production hardware (weatherproofing, solar, LoRa backhaul) and deep learning on sensor time series — threshold rules plus a lightweight statistical model only.

*Outcome:* continuous monitoring of endangered species, rapid response to threats, and long-term habitat records.

Shared foundations that the mobile app, web system and IoT ingestion all depend on.

* Monorepo structure, CI and conventions (see {{README.md}} / {{CLAUDE.md}})
* {{services/api}} (Express) — the single backend for all clients
* {{packages/api-contract}} — OpenAPI spec as the single source of truth, validated at runtime with Zod
* Supabase (database, auth, storage) under {{infra/supabase}}

*Rule:* changes to {{packages/api-contract/}} need two PR approvals because they affect three consumers at once.

Unit deliverables and team process for COS30049, separate from the software itself.

* System Design Proposal (Sprint 1) and its sections
* Sprint planning, reviews and retrospectives
* Client/sponsor communication with NeuonAI and the tutor
* Final report, presentation and demo preparation

As the team, we need the central database and file storage set up in {{infra/supabase/}} so the API has somewhere real to persist data.

*Scope*

* Postgres tables for species, specimens (field records), observations, photos, users/roles, sensor nodes, telemetry, alerts
* Supabase Storage buckets for plant photos and sensor images
* Migrations checked into the repo so every environment can be rebuilt

*Acceptance criteria*

* Schema matches the entities in the OpenAPI contract (CTIP-13)
* Migrations run cleanly on a fresh project
* Storage buckets are private by default; only the API can issue access
* Row Level Security enabled on all tables as a second line of defence
* Seed script with sample Niah species for development

Scaffold the Express app (entry point, config, {{.env.example}} — only {{package.json}} exists right now) and integrate Supabase Auth.

*Scope note:* Sprint 1 assumes internet connectivity is available (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026); build for the normal online case, not offline queuing.

- Integrate Supabase Auth: sign in, issue JWT
- Logout invalidation and token refresh for a reconnecting device
- Public Visitor endpoints that need no token

*Acceptance criteria*
- [ ] Users can sign in via Supabase Auth and receive a JWT
- [ ] Logout invalidates the token
- [ ] Token refresh works for a device reconnecting after being idle
- [ ] Visitor-only public endpoints work without a token

column29:
Draft the initial OpenAPI spec in {{packages/api-contract/}} — the single source of truth for the API, validated at runtime with Zod on the API side.

Cover the core resource shapes (specimens, users/roles, IoT sensor nodes/telemetry) even as stubs, so mobile, web and API work can start against a shared contract instead of guessing at each other's payloads.

Note: changes to {{packages/api-contract/}} need *two approvals* (see CLAUDE.md Conventions) since a change there breaks three consumers at once.

*Prepare for offline later:* Sprint 1 is online-first (lecturer directive, 28 Sep 2026), but create endpoints should already accept a client-generated ID / idempotency key, so resending the same record never creates a duplicate. This keeps offline sync (CTIP-16) from needing an API rework later.

*Acceptance criteria*

* OpenAPI file validates with a linter (e.g. Redocly/Spectral)
* Schemas defined for specimen, observation, user/role, sensor node, telemetry reading, alert
* Endpoints stubbed for specimen CRUD, sync, auth, telemetry ingestion
* Create endpoints accept a client-generated ID; a repeated request returns the existing record instead of a duplicate
* Error response format agreed and documented
* PR approved by two reviewers

Rubric: Process §1 (10 marks). Background, introduction, problem statement, existing solutions, motivations; project objectives and scope. Update from the proposal where scope changed.

column1: Final Report: Project Planning (SWOT, KoST, SSDLC, Risks, Constraints)
column29: Rubric: Process §2 (10 marks). Solution analysis (project forces, SWOT, KoST, SSDLC), risks and constraints. Note risks that actually occurred and how they were handled (e.g. connectivity directive change, Sprint 1 carryover).
Rubric: Process §3 (10 marks). Detailed breakdown of activities, tasks, milestones and key deliverables; schedule overview, delivery phases and timeline. Pull sprint data and burndowns from Jira.

column1: Final Report: System Architecture & Technical Design
column29: Rubric: Process §4 (10 marks). Overall architecture and how it meets requirements; justification of development approach; logical breakdown of features; technical design across hardware, software and interfaces (mobile, web, API, Supabase, IoT/MQTT). Reuse diagrams in {{docs/architecture}}.

column1: Final Report: Testing Plan (Quality Management, Strategy, Environment)
column29: Rubric: Product §1 (10 marks). Quality management (Definition of Done, quality attributes); test strategy listing the tests run, including security testing; test environment (hardware and software).
Rubric: Product §2 (10 marks, shared with security results). Quantitative and qualitative results and analysis, reasoning on outcomes. Use evidence collected in {{docs/testing}} across the sprints.

column1: Final Report: Security Testing Results & Recommendations
column29: Rubric: Product §2 (security testing). Summarise the assess → remediate → reassess cycle: findings from the vulnerability assessment (CTIP-37), remediation (CTIP-50) and reassessment (CTIP-74), with recommendations. Draw on the threat model in {{docs/security}}.

Rubric: Product §3 + §4 (20 marks). How the prototype matches the user needs analysis and shows understanding of the problem; usability against relevant guidelines (task flow and navigation, ease of use for new and experienced users). Include screenshots of mobile and web flows.

Rubric: Product §2 (recommendations for future enhancement). Work not completed (e.g. any offline features that slipped), out-of-scope items such as automated species ID with NeuonAI, production hardware, and a conclusion.
